what: Cencora, formerly AmerisourceBergen, distributes prescription medicines to pharmacies, hospitals and doctors. It specialises in high-value speciality drugs, particularly cancer treatments, and serves manufacturers with logistics and patient services.
customers: Pharmacy chains, hospitals, oncology practices and pharmaceutical manufacturers.
money: distribution of branded, generic and speciality drugs in the United States
distribution in Europe and Canada, and global speciality logistics
moat: Three distributors handle almost all US drug volume; the warehouse and cold-chain network for speciality medicines would cost billions to replicate.
risks: Margins are extremely thin: about one cent on each revenue dollar
A single large customer contract drives much of the volume
Opioid settlement payments continue for years
Drug pricing policy changes how distributors are paid
opportunities: Speciality and oncology drugs grow faster and earn better margins than ordinary distribution
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs push very large volumes through the network
Return on invested capital near 17% is high because it carries little fixed capital
watch: Operating profit by segment, since revenue is dominated by pass-through drug cost.
